intended_object: The Tate cohomology group Ĥ^{-1}(G/S, A^S) of the finite quotient G/S acting on the S-invariants. It is the kernel of the norm N : (A^S)_{G/S} → (A^S)^{G/S} = A^G, viewed as a compact Hausdorff abelian group with the subspace topology from the compact coinvariants. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
How the definition is built:
- `normFromFiniteCoinvariants A L S` is a continuous homomorphism from `finiteCoinvariants A S` to `group A L ⊤`. The source is the coinvariants (A^S)_{G/S}, taken as the quotient by a closed subgroup, so it is compact Hausdorff. The target is A^G with its level topology. On classes the map is the relative norm x ↦ Σ_{g∈G/S} g·x.
- `CompHausAddCommGrp.kernelGroup f` is the kernel of f as a closed subgroup with the induced topology.

So the definition is ker(N_{G/S}) on (A^S)_{G/S}, which is the standard Ĥ^{-1}(G/S, A^S). The topology is the natural compact one.

The same file proves an additive equivalence `tateCohomologyNegOneAddEquivFiniteTate` between this group and the library's algebraic `tateCohomology (A.quotientToInvariants S) (-1)`. This confirms the definition matches the intended object.

The setting is not overly narrow. The compact topology needs a level-compact structure (compact Hausdorff topologies on the invariants A^U). G/S has to be finite so that the norm is defined, which holds because S is open in the compact group G. Mathlib has no topologized Tate cohomology to compare against.
